ac_results.evidence: Exit 0, SMOKE OK. 222 markets (77+77 strike, 2+2 daily updown, 32+32 fast). crypto-term: 316/316 tokens had a book; crypto-fast: 120/128. 63,168 book events and 198 trades. BTC 670 ticks, ETH 698. DVOL BTC 35.49 / ETH 49.65; usdt_usd 0.999455; RTT 207.7 ms. Every kernel feed name was present (polymarket, polymarket:<mode>, binance:BTC/ETH, dvol:BTC/ETH, basis:USDT). Book accuracy: 116,294 of 116,646 price_change messages (99.7%) matched the venue's own best bid/ask. The mismatches were transient (most cleared in 1 message, the longest after 49) and none remained at the end; no book was crossed at the end. All 222 target markets got the right kind and source_id (the crawler regex limits crypto-term slugs to above or up-or-down).

ac_results.ac: C2 Rounding, minimum size, never rounding up and batch limits are tested; setting a live flag raises
ac_results.evidence: Test passes. P4: 200,000 random prices at ticks 0.01 and 0.001 gave 0 roundings that were more aggressive or off-tick (BUY rounds down, SELL rounds up). round_size floors (4.9999999999 -> 4.99; 5.004 -> 5.0). The only 'up' case is 5e-12 shares of float tolerance, which is not a real round-up. 4.999 is refused below the minimum of 5. A batch of 16 raises ValueError; 15 is accepted. LiveTradingForbidden is raised for live=True, for setting router.live, and for TRADER_LIVE set to '1', 'true', 'yes', 'TRUE' or ' on '.

ac_results.ac: C3 Fill-model tests: maker fills on a trade through its price; maker at the touch fills only after queue-ahead plus own size; taker fills at the arrival-time book, partially when size is short; fees correct
ac_results.command: pytest test_maker_fills_on_a_trade_through_its_price, test_maker_at_the_touch_fills_only_after_queue_ahead_plus_own_size_trades, test_taker_fills_at_the_arrival_time_book_partially_with_fees; code read of router.py lines 263-322; probe.py P6/P9/P10
ac_results.evidence: Tests pass. Code: _takers runs before the new book is stored, so a taker fills against the last book received before its arrival. Same-side trades do not move the queue. Trades before created + RTT are ignored (P10: _cum stays empty). P6 with the real trader.fees.fee: taker limit 0.55 fills 2 at 0.50 and kills the rest at 0.60; fee 0.035 = 2*0.07*0.5*0.5. Caveats are listed as minor defects: P1 GTD order, P2 no book at arrival, liquidity reuse, clock mix.

ac_results.ac: C4 Journal: a simulated crash mid-batch, then replay, reproduces every order's state; an unknown order is not retried (test)
ac_results.evidence: _log writes, flushes and fsyncs before state.apply. A 'new' entry is on disk before the 'ack' entries, which are sent after the whole batch. In the test, KeyboardInterrupt fires halfway through the 2nd 'new' line of a batch. After restart, the torn line is ignored, the journaled-but-unacked order and the in-flight taker are 'unknown', and positions and cash are equal. A retry on that token/side is rejected and adds no journal line. Reconcile is clean, and resolve_unknown cancels by id.

ac_results.ac: C5 Reconciler: positions match the fills; an injected mismatch trips a breaker; YES+NO pairs merge (test)
ac_results.command: pytest test_reconciler_matches_fills_trips_on_mismatch_and_merges_pairs; probe2.py with the real trader.kernel.RiskKernel

Injecting +3 shares of drift gives 'position (journal) Y: 13 vs 10'; kernel state becomes HALTED and the trip record has source 'reconciler' ('reconciler' is in PRIVILEGED). merge_pairs merged 10 pairs, cost 9.5, edge 0.5, leaving positions at 0 and cash at +0.5.

ac_results.ac: C6 The measured round trip is logged and used by the taker fill timing
ac_results.command: pytest test_measured_round_trip_sets_taker_arrival_and_is_journaled; cat data/trader/rtt.jsonl; scratch rtt.jsonl from my smoke run
ac_results.evidence: _set_rtt appends each measurement to rtt.jsonl. The builder's runs left 8 lines (202-225 ms; these include the claimed 222.3 and 224.9). My run logged 197.8 and 207.7 ms to scratch. Taker 'new' entries carry arrival_ms = now + 150 + round(rtt) and rtt_ms. In the test, a 400 ms RTT meets a later book than a 100 ms one.
14 passed in 0.57s. The whole trader suite: 109 passed in 8.45s.

defects.description: A GTD-expired maker can still fill. on_trade does not check expiry before filling and calls _expire(ts_ms) only afterwards. Probe P1: a maker with expiry_ms=100000 filled 10 shares on a trade through its price at ts 200000. In live use the window is small, because on_book expires orders on every book event, but a venue-vs-local clock gap widens it.
defects.fix_hint: Call self._expire(ts_ms) at the start of on_trade, or skip makers with o.intent.expiry_ms <= ts_ms in the loop.

defects.description: A taker that reaches arrival with no book in the router is not killed. It waits, then fills against a book received after its arrival, with the fill stamped at arrival time (look-ahead). Probe P2: arrival at 1250, no book; a book arrived at 3000; the fill came at 0.30 with ts 1250. The kernel does not require a book, so whether this happens depends on the engines.
defects.fix_hint: In _takers, when bk is None and arr <= now_ms, log 'done' (FAK with no liquidity) instead of continuing.

defects.description: Our own orders reuse the same displayed liquidity. Two takers on one token both fill the full level (probe3: 5 shown, 10 filled at 0.50). A second maker at the same price does not count our first maker in its queue_ahead. Both make paper results slightly optimistic.
defects.fix_hint: Subtract size already filled at a level from the stored book for the same book snapshot, and add our own resting size at that price to queue_ahead.

defects.description: on_trade mixes two clocks. It compares the venue's server timestamp (last_trade_price.timestamp) against the local created_ms + RTT. If the local clock is behind the venue (Binance receive lag measured -68 to -86 ms), trades from shortly before the order could rest count towards queue progress. The builder already reported this.
defects.fix_hint: Pass the local receive ms (now) as ts_ms to on_trade in MarketData._on_pm, which is conservative, or correct it by the measured server offset.
